newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BICHEL TAKES SIX WICKETS AS NSW CRUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BICHEL TAKES SIX WICKETS AS NSW CRUMBLE.

text.p: Queensland pace bowler Andrew Bichel took six wickets on Thursday as New South Wales collapsed to 190 all out on the opening day of their four-day Sheffield Shield encounter.
Bichel tore through a near test-strength batting order to finish with six for 56, denting the test aspirations of opening batsman Michael Slater in the process.

Slater, dropped from the Australia side at the start of the season, is duelling with Queensland's Matthew Hayden for the Australia opening spot left vacant by the injured Matthew Elliott ahead of next week's third test against West Indies.
He started confidently, hitting pace bowler Michael Kasprowicz for four and six from successive balls only to fall to Bichel soon afterwards for 15.
Hayden also failed later in the day, falling to test fast bowler Glenn McGrath for nine as Queensland reached 89 for two at stumps.

Test opener Mark Taylor and middle-order batsman Michael Bevan were also unable to build big scores, but Waugh, who missed the second test through injury, helped allay concerns about his fitness by top-scoring with 55.
His brother and fellow test player, Mark, played fluently for 31 before he was bowled by paceman Adam Dale for 31.
Bichel has taken four wickets against West Indies twice in the past month, first for an Australian XI and then in Australia A's defeat of the tourists last week.
